episode.title: Frame the Decision: Pragmatic Threat Models

feed.description: Software engineering conversations: reliability, architecture, delivery, and the tradeoffs nobody puts in the blog post.
feed.title: Practical Systems

bullets: Threat modeling is the framing exercise for security design — frame the decision wrong and you build the wrong defenses, a pattern observed across three different teams.
Authentication separation matters more than people think as a security design element — the pattern held consistently across three different teams.
Security incidents are reliability incidents — ignoring that connection leads to rebuilding from scratch a year later, as seen with PagerDuty and Datadog.
Vanta-style compliance work and real security work overlap may be only 60% — internalizing that gap makes the rest of the security decisions easier.
The frame for a security review is what could go wrong if this assumption is wrong — the framing matters because it tells you which tradeoffs you're making.
The second-order effect of security-reliability overlap is the part most people miss — outside of century-class tooling, the failure mode is harder to spot.
A practical next step is to pick one of the covered ideas and run it for two weeks — the rest is iteration.
